summary: What if witnesses say a person ate chelev by mistake? It depends on how many witnesses there are and whether he agrees. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about one case.

chunks.en: If people told him, "You ate chelev,"
chunks.st: If witnesses said to a person: We saw that you ate forbidden fat,

chunks.en: he brings a chatas.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin offering if he did so unwittingly.

chunks.en: If one witness says he ate, and another witness
chunks.st: If a witness says: He ate forbidden fat, and a witness

chunks.en: says he did not eat,
chunks.st: says: He did not eat forbidden fat,

chunks.en: or one woman says he ate, and another woman
chunks.st: or if a woman says: He ate forbidden fat, and a woman

chunks.en: says he did not eat,
chunks.st: says: He did not eat forbidden fat,

chunks.en: he brings an asham taluy.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a provisional guilt offering,
chunks.stMore: brought by one who is uncertain as to whether he committed a sin that requires a sin offering.

words.note: Brought when one is not sure he sinned.

chunks.en: If one witness says he ate, and he himself
chunks.st: If a witness says: He ate forbidden fat, and the person himself

chunks.en: says, "I did not eat,"
chunks.st: says: I did not eat forbidden fat,

chunks.en: he is free. If two witnesses say he ate, and he himself
chunks.st: he is exempt. If two witnesses say: He ate forbidden fat, and the person himself

chunks.en: says, "I did not eat,"
chunks.st: says: I did not eat forbidden fat,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says he must bring a korban.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems him liable to bring a sin offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:
chunks.stMore: This conclusion can be derived a fortiori:

chunks.en: "If two witnesses can bring him to the harsh punishment of death,
chunks.st: If two witnesses could have brought him liability to receive the severe punishment of death,

chunks.en: can't they bring him to a korban, which is lighter?"
chunks.st: can they not bring him liability to sacrifice an offering, which is relatively lenient?

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:
chunks.stMore: Witnesses are unable to render another person liable to bring an offering contrary to his statement,

chunks.he: מָה אִם יִרְצֶה לוֹמַר מֵזִיד הָיִיתִי:
chunks.en: "What if he wants to say, 'I did it on purpose'?"
chunks.explain: Then he would not bring a korban at all.
chunks.st: as what if he wishes to say: I did so intentionally, in which case he would be exempt from bringing an offering?

summary: When does one who eats forbidden foods bring one chatas, and when does he bring many? It depends on whether he ate one kind or many kinds.

chunks.en: If he ate chelev and more chelev in one time of forgetting,
chunks.explain: He did not find out in between that it was forbidden.
chunks.st: If one unwittingly ate an olive-bulk of forbidden fat and then ate another olive-bulk of forbidden fat during one lapse of awareness,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in a case where he did not discover in the interim that fat is forbidden, or that the food he is eating is forbidden fat,

chunks.en: he brings only one chatas.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring only one sin offering.

chunks.en: If he ate chelev, blood, nosar,
chunks.st: If one ate forbidden fat, and blood,

chunks.en: and piggul in one time of forgetting,
chunks.st: and piggul, and notar in one lapse of awareness,

chunks.en: he must bring a chatas for each one.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every one of them.

chunks.he: זֶה חֹמֶר בְּמִינִין הַרְבֵּה מִמִּין אֶחָד.
chunks.en: This is a stricter rule for many kinds than for one kind.
chunks.st: This is a stringency that applies to one who eats several types of forbidden food and does not apply to one who eats one type of forbidden food.

chunks.en: And there is a stricter rule for one kind than for many kinds:
chunks.st: And a stringency that applies to one who eats one type of forbidden food and not to one who eats several types of forbidden food is

chunks.en: if he ate half a kezayis and then
chunks.st: that if one ate half an olive-bulk and then

chunks.en: ate another half a kezayis of the same kind,
chunks.st: ate another half an olive-bulk during one lapse of awareness, in a case where they were both from one type of forbidden food,

chunks.en: he is liable. If from two kinds, he is free.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin offering. If they were from two types, he is exempt,
chunks.stMore: because he did not eat an olive-bulk of any specific forbidden food.

summary: How slowly can a person eat a forbidden food and still be punished? Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue. The same time counts for tamei foods and for drinking wine before going into the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: How long may one take while eating them?
chunks.st: How much time can one expend while eating an olive-bulk of forbidden food and still be liable for violating the prohibition?

chunks.en: As long as it takes to eat roasted grain,
chunks.st: The duration is calculated as though he were eating toasted grain,
chunks.stMore: which one eats one kernel at a time. If he eats the olive-bulk of forbidden food within the amount of time it would take to eat an olive-bulk of toasted grain, he is liable.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: as long as the time from start
chunks.st: Unless the amount of time he expends from beginning to

chunks.en: to end is the time it takes to eat a peras.
chunks.st: end is more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf [peras] of bread, he is liable.

words.note: Half of a loaf of bread.

chunks.en: If one ate tamei foods,
chunks.st: Likewise, one who ate a quarter-loaf of ritually impure foods

chunks.en: or drank tamei drinks,
chunks.st: or drank a quarter-log of ritually impure liquids
chunks.stMore: within the amount of time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread is rendered unfit to partake of teruma, the portion of the produce designated for priests, until he becomes pure.

chunks.en: or drank a revi'is of wine and went into the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one drank a quarter-log of wine and entered the Temple,

words.note: A small amount, about one cup.

chunks.en: and stayed there as long as it takes to eat a peras, he is liable.
chunks.st: and he remained there for the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread, he is liable.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar says:

chunks.en: if he stopped in the middle, or if he put
chunks.st: If he interrupted his drinking of the quarter-log of wine or if he placed

chunks.en: even a little water into it, he is free.
chunks.st: any amount of water into the wine, he is exempt.

summary: One bite of food can make a person bring four chataos and one asham. Rabbi Meir says that on Shabbos it could be even more.

chunks.en: A person can eat one time and must bring
chunks.st: There is a case where one can perform a single act of eating an olive-bulk of food and be liable

chunks.en: four chataos and one asham for it.
chunks.st: to bring four sin offerings and one guilt offering for it.

chunks.en: One who was tamei and ate chelev,
chunks.st: How so? This halakha applies to one who is ritually impure who ate forbidden fat,

chunks.en: and it was nosar,
chunks.st: and it was left over

chunks.en: from korbanos,
chunks.st: from a consecrated offering after the time allotted for its consumption [notar],

chunks.en: and it was Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: on Yom Kippur.
chunks.stMore: He is liable to bring sin offerings for eating forbidden fat and notar, for eating the meat of an offering while impure, and for eating on Yom Kippur. He is also liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: if it was Shabbos and he carried it out in his mouth,
chunks.st: If it was Shabbat and he carried it out from a private domain to a public domain while eating it,

chunks.en: he is liable for one more. They said to him,
chunks.st: he would be liable to bring an additional sin offering for performing prohibited labor on Shabbat. The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: "That is not the same kind of sin."
chunks.st: That liability is not from the same type of prohibition, as it is not due to the act of eating, and therefore, it should not be counted.

summary: One forbidden act can make a person bring six chataos, if the woman is forbidden to him in many ways at once.

chunks.en: A person can do one forbidden act
chunks.st: There is a case where one can engage in a single act of intercourse

chunks.en: and must bring six chataos for it.
chunks.st: and be liable to bring six sin offerings for it.

chunks.en: One who sins with his daughter
chunks.st: How so? It is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his daughter

chunks.en: must bring for her because she is his daughter, his sister,
chunks.st: to be liable due to having violated the prohibitions of engaging in intercourse with his daughter, his sister,

chunks.en: his brother's wife, his father's brother's wife,
chunks.st: the wife of his brother, the wife of his father’s brother,

chunks.en: a married woman, and a niddah.
chunks.st: a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: And one who sins with his daughter's daughter
chunks.st: It is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his daughter’s daughter to be

chunks.he: חַיָּב עָלֶיהָ מִשּׁוּם בַּת בִּתּוֹ וְכַלָּתוֹ
chunks.en: must bring for her because she is his daughter's daughter, his daughter-in-law,
chunks.st: liable to bring sin offerings due to the unwitting violation of the prohibitions of engaging in intercourse with his daughter’s daughter, and his daughter-in-law,

chunks.he: וַאֲחוֹת אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֵשֶׁת אָחִיו וְאֵשֶׁת אֲחִי
chunks.en: his wife's sister, his brother's wife, the wife of his father's
chunks.st: and the wife of his brother,

chunks.en: brother, a married woman, and a niddah.
chunks.st: and the wife of his father’s brother, and his wife’s sister, and a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: if the grandfather broke the law and married her,
chunks.st: If the elder, i.e., the man’s father, who is the woman’s great-grandfather, transgressed and married her,

chunks.en: he must also bring for her because she is his father's wife.
chunks.st: the man would also be liable for engaging in intercourse with her due to the prohibition of intercourse with the wife of his father.

chunks.en: And the same for one who sins with his wife's daughter,
chunks.st: And likewise, it is possible for one who engages in intercourse with the daughter of his wife
chunks.stMore: to be liable to bring six sin offerings, similar to one who engages in intercourse with his own daughter, for violating the prohibitions against engaging in intercourse with his wife’s daughter, his sister, the wife of his brother, the wife of his father’s brother, a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: or with his wife's daughter's daughter.
chunks.st: And it is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his wife’s daughter’s daughter to be liable to bring seven sin offerings, similar to one who engages in intercourse with his own daughter’s daughter, for violating the following prohibitions: Engaging in intercourse with his wife’s daughter’s daughter, his daughter-in-law, the wife of his brother, the wife of his father’s brother, his wife’s sister, a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

summary: One who sins with his mother-in-law can be forbidden to her in many ways at once. Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri and the Sages argue whether some of them count as separate sins.

chunks.en: One who sins with his mother-in-law
chunks.st: It is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his mother-in-law

chunks.en: must bring for her because she is his mother-in-law, his daughter-in-law,
chunks.st: to be liable to bring seven sin offerings for doing so, due to the unwitting violation of the prohibitions of engaging in intercourse with his mother-in-law, and his daughter-in-law,

chunks.en: his wife's sister, his brother's wife, the wife
chunks.st: and the wife of his brother,

chunks.en: of his father's brother, a married woman, and a niddah.
chunks.st: and the wife of his father’s brother, and his wife’s sister, and a married woman, and a menstruating woman.

chunks.en: And the same for one who sins with his mother-in-law's mother,
chunks.st: And likewise, the same applies with regard to one who engages in intercourse with the mother of his father-in-law

chunks.en: or with his father-in-law's mother.
chunks.st: or with the mother of his mother-in-law.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says:

chunks.en: one who sins with his mother-in-law
chunks.st: It is possible for one who engages in intercourse with his mother-in-law

chunks.en: must bring for her because she is his mother-in-law,
chunks.st: to be liable due to the unwitting violation of the prohibitions of engaging in intercourse with his mother-in-law,

chunks.en: his mother-in-law's mother, and his father-in-law's mother.
chunks.st: and the mother of his mother-in-law, and the mother of his father-in-law.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him:

chunks.en: "All three of them are one kind of sin."
chunks.st: Those three prohibitions are all one category
chunks.stMore: of prohibition, derived from the same verse: “You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter; you shall not take her son’s daughter, or her daughter’s daughter” (Leviticus 18:17). Consequently, one is not liable to bring separate sin offerings for violating these prohibitions.

summary: Rabbi Akiva asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua: if a person did several different forbidden things in one time of forgetting, does he bring one chatas or one for each? They answered from a similar case they had heard.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: "I asked Rabban Gamliel and
chunks.st: I asked Rabban Gamliel and

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua in the meat market of Emmaus,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua in the meat market [itlis] in Emmaus,

chunks.en: where they went to buy an animal for the wedding feast
chunks.st: where they went to purchase an animal for the wedding feast

chunks.en: of Rabban Gamliel's son:
chunks.st: of the son of Rabban Gamliel:

chunks.he: הַבָּא עַל אֲחוֹתוֹ וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו
chunks.en: One who sins with his sister, and with his father's sister,
chunks.st: In the case of one who unwittingly engages in intercourse with his sister, and the sister of his father,

chunks.he: וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד מַהוּ,
chunks.en: and with his mother's sister, in one time of forgetting, what is the rule?
chunks.st: and the sister of his mother, during one lapse of awareness, what is the halakha?

chunks.en: Must he bring one chatas for all of them,
chunks.st: Is he liable to bring one sin offering for all three prohibitions,

chunks.he: אוֹ אַחַת עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת,
chunks.en: or one for each and every one?
chunks.st: or is he liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of the prohibitions?

chunks.en: And they said to me,
chunks.st: They said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: 'We did not hear about this.
chunks.st: We did not hear a ruling from our teachers about that case,

chunks.en: But we did hear
chunks.st: but we heard the following ruling:

chunks.en: that one who was with his five wives
chunks.st: One who engages in intercourse with each of his five wives

chunks.en: when they were niddah, in one time of forgetting,
chunks.st: while they are menstruating, during one lapse of awareness,

chunks.he: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
chunks.en: must bring a chatas for each and every one.'
chunks.st: we heard that he is liable to bring a separate sin offering for having engaged in intercourse with each and every one of them.

chunks.en: And it seems to me that these things are a kal vachomer."
chunks.st: And it appears to me that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference:
chunks.stMore: If he is liable to bring separate sin offerings for having engaged in intercourse with five menstruating women, who are forbidden by one prohibition, he should certainly be liable to bring separate sin offerings for having engaged in intercourse with his sister, the sister of his father, and the sister of his mother, who are forbidden by three separate prohibitions.

words.note: Kal vachomer: if a rule is true in an easier case, it is surely true in a harder one.

summary: Rabbi Akiva asked whether a limb of an animal that is hanging loose makes things tamei. The Rabbis answered from what sick people in Yerushalayim used to do before Pesach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva asked them another question:
chunks.st: And furthermore, Rabbi Akiva asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua in the meat market of Emmaus:

chunks.en: A limb of an animal that is hanging loose,
chunks.st: What is the status of a dangling limb of an animal?
chunks.stMore: Does it impart ritual impurity like a severed limb?

chunks.en: what is the rule? They said to him,
chunks.st: They said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: "We did not hear about this.
chunks.st: We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case,

chunks.en: But we did hear about a limb of a person that is hanging loose,
chunks.st: but we have heard with regard to a dangling limb of a person

chunks.en: that it is tahor.
chunks.st: that it is ritually pure.

chunks.he: שֶׁכָּךְ הָיוּ מֻכֵּי שְׁחִין שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם עוֹשִׂין,
chunks.en: This is what people sick with boils in Yerushalayim used to do:
chunks.st: And in this manner would the people afflicted with boils, whose limbs were dangling due to their affliction, act in Jerusalem:

chunks.he: הוֹלֵךְ לוֹ עֶרֶב פֶּסַח אֵצֶל הָרוֹפֵא
chunks.en: one would go to the doctor on Erev Pesach,
chunks.st: Each of them would go on Passover eve to the doctor,

chunks.he: וְחוֹתְכוֹ עַד שֶׁהוּא מַנִּיחַ בּוֹ כִשְׂעֹרָה,
chunks.en: and the doctor cuts it almost all the way, leaving only a hair's width,
chunks.st: who would cut the affected limb almost completely until he would leave it connected by a hairbreadth of flesh,
chunks.stMore: so that neither the doctor nor the afflicted would be rendered ritually impure by a severed limb.

chunks.en: and sticks it onto a thorn,
chunks.st: Then, the doctor would impale the limb on a thorn
chunks.stMore: attached to the floor or the wall,

chunks.en: and the sick man pulls away from it.
chunks.st: and the afflicted would pull away from the thorn,
chunks.stMore: thereby completely severing the limb.

chunks.en: Then that man brings his Korban Pesach,
chunks.st: And that person afflicted with boils would perform the rite of his Paschal offering,

chunks.en: and the doctor brings his Korban Pesach.
chunks.st: and the doctor would perform the rite of his Paschal offering,
chunks.stMore: as neither had come into contact with the limb once it was severed. In any case, as long as it was dangling, the limb did not impart impurity.

chunks.en: And it seems to us that these things are a kal vachomer."
chunks.st: And I consider that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference.
chunks.stMore: If a person’s limb, the impurity of which when amputated is severe, does not impart impurity when it is dangling, it is all the more so logical that an animal’s limb, the impurity of which when amputated is lenient, does not impart impurity when it is dangling.

summary: Rabbi Akiva asked about one who did the same sin with five korbanos in one time of forgetting. Rabbi Yehoshua answered from the rule of me'ilah, but Rabbi Akiva showed why that proof does not work.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva asked them another question:

chunks.en: They said to him,

chunks.en: "We did not hear about this."
chunks.st: We have not heard a ruling from our teachers in that specific case.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.st: I have heard with regard to one who eats meat from one offering

chunks.st: from five different pots in which they were prepared, during one lapse of awareness,

chunks.en: that he must bring a korban for each
chunks.st: that he is liable to bring five guilt offerings, which are for the meat prepared in each

chunks.st: I have heard with regard to one who eats meat from one offering

chunks.st: that he is liable to bring separate guilt offerings for the meat prepared in each

chunks.st: and every pot, due to misuse of consecrated property.

chunks.en: And I see that these things are a kal vachomer.'
chunks.st: And I consider that these matters can be derived from an a fortiori inference:
chunks.stMore: If one is liable to bring five guilt offerings for one offering prepared in five pots, all the more so is he liable to bring five sin offerings for eating the notar of five separate offerings.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: 'If it is a halachah you received,
chunks.st: If you are reporting a halakha that you received from your teachers

chunks.en: He said to him,

chunks.en: 'Answer!' He said to him,

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בִמְעִילָה שֶׁעָשָׂה בָהּ אֶת

chunks.en: one who feeds others like one who eats, and one who lets others benefit like one who benefits,
chunks.st: As, with regard to misuse, the Torah established that the status of one who feeds another person sacrificial meat is like that of one who eats sacrificial meat, and the status of one who gives benefit to another from consecrated property that is not food is like that of one who derives benefit himself,
chunks.stMore: in that each is liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse.

chunks.en: and joined me'ilah over a long time,
chunks.st: In addition, the Torah joined the misuse of consecrated property that was performed over an extended period,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if one derived benefit worth half a peruta one day and half a peruta the next, he is liable to bring a guilt offering for misuse.

summary: Rabbi Akiva asked Rabbi Eliezer about one who does many melachos of the same kind on many Shabbosos in one time of forgetting. Rabbi Eliezer tried to prove that he brings many chataos, and Rabbi Akiva answered each proof.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: "I asked Rabbi Eliezer:
chunks.st: I asked Rabbi Eliezer with regard to

chunks.en: One who does many melachos on many Shabbosos,
chunks.st: one who performs multiple prohibited labors on several Shabbatot,

chunks.en: all of the same kind of melachah,
chunks.st: and all those labors were subsumed as subcategories of one primary category of prohibited labor,

chunks.en: in one time of forgetting,
chunks.st: and he performed them during one lapse of awareness.

chunks.en: what is the rule?
chunks.st: What is the halakha?

chunks.en: Must he bring one chatas for all of them,
chunks.st: Is he liable to bring one sin offering for unwitting performance of all these labors

chunks.he: אוֹ אַחַת עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
chunks.en: or one for each and every one?'
chunks.st: or is he liable to bring a sin offering for violation of each and every one of the labors?

chunks.en: He said to me,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Akiva:

chunks.en: 'He must bring one for each and every one,
chunks.st: He is liable to bring a sin offering for violation of each and every one of the labors,

chunks.en: from a kal vachomer:
chunks.st: and this is derived from an a fortiori inference:

chunks.en: If for a niddah,
chunks.st: Just as in the case of a menstruating woman,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְחַטָּאוֹת הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: where there are not many kinds of sins and many chataos,
chunks.st: with regard to whom there are not multiple actions that result in transgression and that result in multiple sin offerings,
chunks.stMore: but rather only the prohibition against engaging in intercourse with her,

chunks.en: one must bring a chatas for each time,
chunks.st: and nevertheless one is liable to bring a separate sin offering for each and every one of his acts of unwitting intercourse;

chunks.he: שַׁבָּת, שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ תּוֹצָאוֹת הַרְבֵּה וְחַטָּאוֹת הַרְבֵּה,
chunks.en: then Shabbos, where there are many kinds of sins and many chataos,
chunks.st: in the case of Shabbat, with regard to which there are multiple primary categories and subcategories of labor that result in transgression and that result in multiple death penalties or sin offerings,

chunks.en: isn't it right that he must bring
chunks.st: is it not right that he will be liable

chunks.en: one for each and every one?'
chunks.st: to bring a sin offering for performance of each and every one of the prohibited labors?

chunks.en: I said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva continues: I said to Rabbi Eliezer that the inference is not valid:

chunks.en: 'No! If you said this about a niddah,
chunks.st: If you said one is liable to bring multiple sin offerings in the case of a menstruating woman,

chunks.en: where there are two warnings,
chunks.st: with regard to whom there are two prohibitions,

chunks.en: since he is warned about the niddah
chunks.st: as the man is prohibited from engaging in intercourse with the menstruating woman

chunks.en: and the niddah is warned about him,
chunks.st: and the menstruating woman is prohibited from engaging in intercourse with him,

chunks.en: will you say the same about Shabbos,
chunks.st: would you say the same in the case of Shabbat,

chunks.en: where there is only one warning?'
chunks.st: with regard to which there is only one prohibition?

chunks.en: He said to me,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to me:

chunks.en: 'The case of young girls who are niddah will prove it,
chunks.st: The halakha of one who engages in intercourse with minor menstruating girls will prove
chunks.stMore: this refutation is not valid,

chunks.en: where there is only one warning,
chunks.st: as in that case there is only one prohibition,
chunks.stMore: because the minor is exempt from the mitzvot,

chunks.en: and still he must bring one for each and every time.'
chunks.st: and nevertheless the man is liable to bring a separate sin offering for intercourse for each and every one of the acts of intercourse.

chunks.en: I said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said: I said to Rabbi Eliezer that the cases of Shabbat and minor menstruating girls are not comparable.

chunks.he: לֹא, אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַּבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנּוֹת,
chunks.en: 'No! If you said this about the young girls,
chunks.st: If you said in the case of minor girls

chunks.he: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן עַכְשָׁיו,
chunks.en: that even though there is no warning for them now,
chunks.st: that although it is not prohibited for them at present

chunks.en: there will be later,
chunks.st: it is prohibited for them after the passage of time, when they reach majority,

chunks.en: will you say the same about Shabbos,
chunks.st: would you say the same in the case of Shabbat,

chunks.en: where there is not, not now
chunks.st: with regard to which there are neither two prohibitions at present, nor

chunks.en: and not later?'
chunks.st: will there be after the passage of time?

chunks.en: He said to me,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to me:

chunks.en: 'One who sins with an animal will prove it.'
chunks.st: The halakha of one who copulates with an animal will prove
chunks.stMore: this refutation is not valid, as there are never two prohibitions in that case, and nevertheless the person is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every act.

chunks.en: I said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said: I said to Rabbi Eliezer that no proof can be cited from the case of an animal,

chunks.en: 'An animal is like Shabbos.'"
chunks.st: as in my opinion the case of the animal is like that of Shabbat;
chunks.stMore: there is uncertainty with regard to both cases.
